\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{تعریف} (tārīf)}{تعریف (tārīf)}]{\ur{تعریف} (tārīf) — praise}

\label{lesson:UR-C355-tarif}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for a groundless fear, then the Urdu for unwarranted.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{تعریف}}
\textbf{\ur{تعریف}} — \emph{tārīf} — \textquotedblleft{}praise\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{استاد} \ur{نے} \ur{سارا} \ur{کی} \ur{تعریف} \ur{کی۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{ustād ne sārā kī tārīf kī.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The teacher praised Sara.
\end{quote}

Feminine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{تعریف}} (\emph{tārīf}) is usually traced, through Persian, to Arabic \emph{taʿrīf}, \textquotedblleft{}making known, description\textquotedblright{}; Urdu uses it for describing someone well, \textquotedblleft{}praise\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for giving reasons and opinions.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{tārīf}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{tārīf}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ustād ne sārā kī tārīf kī.} — The teacher praised Sara.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for a groundless fear, then the Urdu for unwarranted, then say \emph{tārīf} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ur{تعریف} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Praise\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{قصور} (qusūr)}{قصور (qusūr)}]{\ur{قصور} (qusūr) — fault; blame}

\label{lesson:UR-C355-qusur}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for unwarranted, then the Urdu for praise.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{سراہنا} (sarāhnā)}{سراہنا (sarāhnā)}]{\ur{سراہنا} (sarāhnā) — to commend; to praise}

\label{lesson:UR-C355-sarahna}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for fault, then the Urdu for reproach.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{سراہنا}}
\textbf{\ur{سراہنا}} — \emph{sarāhnā} — \textquotedblleft{}to commend; to praise\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{سب} \ur{نے} \ur{اس} \ur{کے} \ur{کام} \ur{کو} \ur{سراہا۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{sab ne us ke kām ko sarāhā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Everyone praised her work.
\end{quote}

Past, with \ur{نے} (he or she …): \ur{اس} \ur{نے} \ur{کوشش} \ur{کو} \ur{سراہا}, \emph{us ne koshish ko sarāhā}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{سراہنا}} (\emph{sarāhnā}) is inherited: CDIAL lists the Hindi cousin \emph{sarāhnā} under Sanskrit \emph{ślāghate}, \textquotedblleft{}praises\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 12734).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for giving reasons and opinions.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{جھیلنا} (jhelnā)}{جھیلنا (jhelnā)}]{\ur{جھیلنا} (jhelnā) — to endure; to put up with}

\label{lesson:UR-C355-jhelna}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for reproach, then the Urdu for to commend.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{جھیلنا}}
\textbf{\ur{جھیلنا}} — \emph{jhelnā} — \textquotedblleft{}to endure; to put up with\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{کسانوں} \ur{نے} \ur{سخت} \ur{سردی} \ur{جھیلی۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{kisānoṅ ne sakht sardī jhelī.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The farmers endured a hard winter.
\end{quote}

Past, with \ur{نے} (he or she …): \ur{اس} \ur{نے} \ur{سردی} \ur{جھیلی}, \emph{us ne sardī jhelī}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{جھیلنا}} (\emph{jhelnā}) is inherited: CDIAL lists the Hindi cousin \emph{jhelnā} under \emph{*jhēlati}, \textquotedblleft{}undergoes\textquotedblright{}, a form it reconstructs (CDIAL 5413).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for giving reasons and opinions.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for reproach, then the Urdu for to commend, then say \emph{jhelnā} again
\end{itemize}
